title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-wip
content:
Context:
Personal scratchpad while investigating an ongoing observability pipeline problem impacting tracing, metrics and logs for the hosted-api cluster in us-west-2. Symptoms: sudden drop in Prometheus scrape metrics (service throughput metrics) around 2026-02-27 08:14 UTC, partial loss of Jaeger traces (sampling drops to near 0 for some services), and a backlog / delay in Loki log ingestion for mariadb/gateway pods. Intermittent errors in OTEL collector reported in logs.

High-level hypothesis:
- OTEL collector config or resource pressure caused batching/backpressure and then timeouts -> metric export drop + trace flush failures.
- Network flapping between collector agents and central ingest (TLS handshake timeouts) for a subset of nodes.
- Recent roll of collector config (PR #48) might have introduced a config that disables a processor or changed export timeout.

Timeline / quick events:
- 2026-02-27 08:10 UTC: Alert fired (INF-4321) - prometheus scrape error rate increased.
- 2026-02-27 08:14 UTC: Metrics drop observed in grafana - host and route-level token counts down 70%.
- 2026-02-27 08:20 UTC: First jaeger sampling anomalies reported from internal canary.
- 2026-02-27 08:32 UTC: Loki ingestion backlog spikes on shipper nodes.
- 2026-02-27 09:05 UTC: Rolled a restart of otel-collector daemonset on cluster-a for testing.

Commands tried (notes + outputs summarized):
1) Check OTEL collector pods / restarts:
   kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=otel-collector -o wide
   -> several pods on cluster-a show RESTARTS=3 in last 24h, Age 2d.

2) Inspect otel logs (collector) for recent errors:
   kubectl -n observability logs otel-collector-5f7b9 -c otel-collector --since=2h | tail -n 200
   -> repeated: "exporter failed to send batch: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed"
   -> also: "timeout while waiting for response from prometheus exporter: context deadline exceeded"

3) Check network connectivity to central-ingest endpoint from agent node (pod exec):
   curl -v https://ingest.internal.redwood:4317 --max-time 5
   -> TLS handshake failed intermittently (sometimes succeeds).

4) List open file descriptors / ulimit on otel pod (hypothesis: fd leak):
   kubectl -n observability exec -it otel-collector-5f7b9 -- bash -c 'ls -1 /proc/1/fd | wc -l; ulimit -n'
   -> fd count ~ 1024, ulimit 4096. Not obviously exhausted but possible slow leak over time.

5) Check Prometheus scrape errors and latency:
   curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROM_QUERY_TOKEN" "https://prometheus-usw2.redwood/api/v1/query?query=rate(prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds_count[5m])" | jq .
   -> spikes in scrape duration and increased 5xx on /metrics endpoints for certain pods (gateway-*).

6) Grafana / traces check:
   - Quick jaeger query for service=gateway, operation=forwardRequest shows traces dropped after 08:12.

Error snippets collected:
- "exporter failed to send batch: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed"
- "context deadline exceeded" when pushing spans to OTLP gRPC exporter
- Loki shipper: "failed to push chunk: client returned HTTP status 500" (sporadic)
- Prometheus scrape: 502/504 on kube-proxy logs for some target IPs

Evidence pointing at network instability/backpressure:
- TLS handshake failures to central ingest
- gRPC Unavailable errors from exporter
- Partial success when restarting collector pod -> metrics/traces start flowing for 10-15m then degrade again

Recent changes to check:
- Merge of OTEL collector config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-collector-config/pull/48 -> changed exporter retry_policy and timeout from 10s -> 2s (intended to reduce tail latency). Could be too aggressive causing drops when transient latency occurs.
- Firewall rule update in us-west-2 happened 2026-02-26 17:00 UTC (infra slack thread) - double-check if applied to all subnets.

Short experiments performed (and outcome):
- Increased exporter timeout locally in pod (env OTEL_EXPORTER_TIMEOUT=15s) then restarted pod -> immediate improvement: collector showed fewer Unavailable errors and Prometheus scrape success returned for that node.
- Temporarily disabled batching processor (set batch.timeout to 200ms -> 0ms) -> mixed results; batching reduces number of connections but increases latency.
- Restarted kube-proxy on one affected node -> reduced 502 errors for targets on that node for ~20m.

Hypotheses refined:
1) The PR reducing timeout to 2s made the collector intolerant to transient network hiccups; exporters give up quickly leading to dropped spans/metrics and build-up/backpressure in pipeline.
2) There is intermittent network latency or TLS handshake failures between agent collectors and central ingest (load balancer or NAT gateway flapping).
3) Some nodes have kube-proxy or iptables issues causing 502/504 to /metrics endpoints and Loki shipper failing to push chunks.
4) Resource pressure (burst CPU) on collector sidecar could amplify these issues when combined with low timeouts.

Immediate mitigation steps taken / proposed:
- Revert or patch PR #48 to restore exporter timeout to 10s while we stabilize network. (done on a single canary cluster; monitoring)
- Increase readiness/liveness probe thresholds for otel-collector to avoid rapid restarts under transient errors.
- Add a temporary circuit breaker / local buffering for Loki shipper and OTEL exporter so spikes do not backpressure producers.
- Infra to validate load balancer and NAT gateway health across us-west-2 (ticketed infra).

Next diagnostic actions:
- Collect tcpdump on an affected node during a degradation window:
   kubectl -n observability exec -it otel-collector-5f7b9 -- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/otel-conn.pcap port 4317 and host ingest.internal.redwood & sleep 300; pkill -f tcpdump
   -> upload pcap to S3 for analysis.
- Enable debug-level logs temporarily on otel-collector for backoff/retry metrics and exporter diagnostics.
- Run a controlled load test to reproduce: generate span/metric load from canary service and monitor exporter behavior with the 2s vs 10s timeout.
- Check kube-proxy and iptables versions on affected nodes and correlate with 502/504 errors.

Follow-ups / notes to self:
- Sync with infra (Riley) to check LB/NAT health and firewall rules.
- Coordinate with Maya to revert PR at org repo if canary shows improvement after timeout change.
- Add an observability runbook entry summarizing this class of failure (collector timeout vs network instability).

Quick logs excerpts (raw):
[2026-02-27T08:12:34Z] otel-collector ERROR exporter/exporter.go:93 exporter failed to send batch: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
[2026-02-27T08:13:01Z] prometheus TARGET gateway-12 /metrics 502 bad gateway
[2026-02-27T08:14:05Z] loki shipper WARN shipper.go:412 failed to push chunk: client returned HTTP status 500

Notes on long-term fixes:
- Consider tuning the exporter retry policy to be more adaptive (exponential backoff with jitter) rather than short fixed timeout.
- Improve canary coverage for observability pipeline (small synthetic trace/metric producer across all zones to detect early signal).
- Investigate possibility of adding regional buffering for traces/metrics to tolerate central ingest transient errors.

Status: currently monitoring canary after canary rollback to 10s timeout; initial canary node shows stable metrics/traces for ~25m. Will update INF-4321 and this note as we progress.

-- Evan
